This is very shallow analysis that does not discuss the complexities and scale of internation trade. US imports in 2016 were 13 billion more than they were in 2011 (69.6b vs 56.6b) and exports to korea were 1 billion less. For comparison, US imports from China in 2016 were higher than in 2011 by 63.6b (462.8b vs 399.4b) which is more than all imports from Korea in 2011, and US imports from Japan in 2016 were higher than in 2011 by 3.1b (132b vs 128.9b). The economy of the US is huge and slight shifts in consumption behavior, such as substituting imports from China or Mexico with imports from Korea, could easily account for that 13 billion dollar difference. Yeah, imports from China also increased, but who's to say they wouldnt have been higher if we had continued to have higher tariffs for Korea than we did for these other countries?

You can also look at the types of goods that were imported by country. Looking at those numbers you could say that the entire 13b increase was due to auto and pharmaceutical imports because those look like the categories with the biggest changes, but percentage-wise there are big ups and big downs all over the place. Again though, a change in a category doesnt necessarily mean that US-made goods "won" or "lost" as a result of an increase or decrease of imports from Korea because consumers in the US might have just been importing from Korea instead of importing from somewhere else.
